sources_read: .qc-cache/coldwater-editor-2026-10-02-r1/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx:Internal Quality Checks row 29; Deterministic Checks sheet
evidence: Static pairwise review of all 31 criteria (3 gates, 28 scored) found no incompatible products or separately rewarded duplicate outcome. The closest overlap is Constraints cw_shared_saved_record at tests/gates/constraints/judge.toml:27-32, which proves an application write and independent-context readback, versus Functional cw_save_reload_restart at tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:198-203, which uses that successful save/readback as the control for the distinct process-restart durability promise in environment/instructions/behaviour.md. The gate has zero reward mass (tests/scoring.toml:1-3); the functional criterion requires a completed restart and preserved identity, revision, fields and history. Functional cw_stale_save_draft_safety and cw_history_restore_retry (functional/judge.toml:207-221) test different outcomes: refusal with dirty-draft retention versus a new historical head and retry idempotence. JS and HTML formatting rows (functional/judge.toml:126-140) use different source languages; timeout supersession (functional/judge.toml:180-185) is distinct from last-good input/canvas restoration (functional/judge.toml:171-176). Visual criteria explicitly separate editor readability, pane geometry and component finish (tests/scored/visual/judge.toml:18-45). Counterfactual probes: a localStorage-only save may survive same-context reload but fails the clean-context server-response gate; an otherwise compliant editor with an unconventional palette is allowed by the token criteria and may receive an independent visual-quality judgment. No false pass or false fail from criterion conflict was demonstrated. The raw-evidence index is absent, so no full configured judge observation corroborates these static conclusions; runtime risk remains.
